questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Whether too many people cause climate change
How to reduce your electricity bill at home
Why people in India shop so much these days
How the world's population is counted
questions.why: Neil says they'll discuss the controversial link between overpopulation and climate change.

questions.q: What does Sam give as the obvious cause of climate change?
options: Natural changes in the weather
Carbon emissions from human activities
Too many animals
Cutting down forests only
questions.why: She says climate change is the result of carbon emissions caused by humans.

questions.q: Why is the link between population and emissions 'not so simple'?
options: Because the population is falling
Because nobody knows the real population
Because people don't all produce the same amount of carbon
Because emissions have nothing to do with people
questions.why: Sam says not everyone emits carbon equally; westerners produce far more.

questions.q: According to Professor Arvind Ravikumar, how much would two billion extra low-income people raise emissions?
options: By more than 60%
By about 15%
They would double them
By just 1.5%
questions.why: Neal Razzell says they would see global emissions rise by just 1.5%.

questions.q: What point do the presenters make with Professor Ravikumar's figures?
options: Where you are born makes a big difference to your emissions
Poor countries are the main cause of climate change
Population growth has no effect at all
Everyone should stop using cars
questions.why: Neal Razzell concludes: 'where you were born matters'.

questions.q: According to this view, what is the real problem?
options: Overpopulation
Lack of electricity
Consuming too much
Poor education
questions.why: Neil says the real problem is not overpopulation but overconsumption.

questions.q: How does Priti Dhagan feel about her shopping?
options: She feels guilty and wants to stop
She is not sorry, because it makes her happy
She shops only for her family
She thinks she buys too little
questions.why: She says she loves it and is 'not apologetic about it'.

questions.q: What does Priti mean when she talks about her brain and heart?
options: Her brain tells her to buy more things
Her heart tells her to help the poor
Both agree that she should shop much less
She knows she should feel sorry but doesn't
questions.why: She says the brain says yes, we should be apologetic, but the heart does not agree.
